parts.zh: W: 谢谢你在这么短的时间内抽空见我
W: 确实同意了。我希望签署协议
M: 好吧，没问题。那么你想做什么改动？
W: 基本上，我们希望新协议不包括中东地区
W: 我的客户还收到几家中东公司的其他潜在营销合作邀约
M: 你说的中东业务具体属于哪个行业？

items.stem: What does the woman say she will do?

choices.text: Reply to the man's last proposal within a short time.
choices.zh: 在短时间内回复男士的最新提议。

choices.text: Sign the agreement if one small change is made to it.
choices.zh: 如果对协议做一处小的修改就签署协议。

choices.text: Make a sponsorship deal for her client at the meeting.
choices.zh: 在会议上为她的客户达成一项赞助协议。

choices.text: Give the man some good news regarding the contract.
choices.zh: 告诉男士一些关于合同的好消息。

items.stem: What does the man say about some people he represents?

choices.text: They are becoming impatient.
choices.zh: 他们正变得不耐烦。

choices.text: They are afraid time is running out.
choices.zh: 他们担心时间不多了。

choices.text: They are used to making alterations.
choices.zh: 他们习惯于做出修改。

choices.text: They are concerned about the details.
choices.zh: 他们关注细节。

items.stem: What reason does the woman give for the new deal to exclude the Middle East?

choices.text: To prevent geographical discrimination.
choices.zh: 为了防止地域歧视。

choices.text: To tap the food and beverage market.
choices.zh: 为了开拓食品和饮料市场。

choices.text: To avoid any conflict of interest.
choices.zh: 为了避免任何利益冲突。

choices.text: To reduce unfair competition.
choices.zh: 为了减少不公平竞争。

items.stem: What does the man say about the Middle East?

choices.text: It is a potential market for food and beverage.
choices.zh: 它是食品和饮料的潜在市场。

choices.text: It is very attractive for real estate developers.
choices.zh: 它对房地产开发商很有吸引力。

choices.text: It is a negligible market for his company.
choices.zh: 对他的公司来说它是一个微不足道的市场。

choices.text: It is very different from other markets.
choices.zh: 它与其他市场非常不同。

items.stem: What does the woman say about all the astronomers at the Denver Observatory?

choices.text: They are thrilled by a rare astronomic phenomenon.
choices.zh: 他们对一种罕见的天文现象感到兴奋。

choices.text: They are celebrating a big event on mountain tops.
choices.zh: 他们正在山顶庆祝一个重大事件。

choices.text: They are enthusiastic about big science-related stories.
choices.zh: 他们对与科学相关的重大新闻充满热情。

choices.text: They are joined by astronomers all across North America.
choices.zh: 北美各地的天文学家都加入了他们。

items.stem: What do we learn from the conversation about the Oppenheimer comet?

choices.text: It will be the most formidable of its kind in over a century.
choices.zh: 它将是一个多世纪以来同类中最壮观的。

choices.text: It will come closest to Earth in more than one hundred years.
choices.zh: 它将在一百多年来最接近地球。

choices.text: It will eclipse many other such events in human history.
choices.zh: 它将使人类历史上许多其他此类事件黯然失色。

choices.text: It will be seen most clearly from Denver's mountain tops.
choices.zh: 从丹佛的山顶将最清楚地看到它。

items.stem: What does the woman say people will only see in the sky without a telescope?

choices.text: blur.
choices.zh: 模糊的影像。

choices.text: Stars.
choices.zh: 星星。

choices.text: The edge of our galaxy.
choices.zh: 我们星系的边缘。

choices.text: An ordinary flying object.
choices.zh: 一个普通的飞行物体。

items.stem: What do scientists at the Denver Observatory advise amateurs do to facilitate their observation?

choices.text: Use professional equipment.
choices.zh: 使用专业设备。

choices.text: Climb to the nearby heights.
choices.zh: 爬到附近的高处。

choices.text: Fix their eyes due north.
choices.zh: 将目光固定在正北方。

choices.text: Make use of phone apps.
choices.zh: 使用手机应用程序。

items.stem: What question is said to have recently stirred debate?

choices.text: Whether consumers should be warned against ultra-processed foods.
choices.zh: 是否应该警告消费者不要食用超加工食品。

choices.text: Whether there is sufficient scientific consensus on dietary guidelines.
choices.zh: 关于膳食指南是否存在充分的科学共识。

choices.text: Whether guidelines can form the basis for nutrition advice to consumers.
choices.zh: 指南能否构成向消费者提供营养建议的基础。

choices.text: Whether food scientists will agree on the concept of ultra-processed foods.
choices.zh: 食品科学家是否会就超加工食品的概念达成一致。

items.stem: How does the system developed by Monteiro and colleagues classify foods?

choices.text: By the labor cost for the final products.
choices.zh: 按最终产品的人工成本。

choices.text: By the degree of industrial processing.
choices.zh: 按工业加工程度。

choices.text: By the extent of chemical alteration.
choices.zh: 按化学改变程度。

choices.text: By the convention of classification.
choices.zh: 按分类惯例。

items.stem: What is consumption of ultra-processed foods linked with, according to studies?

choices.text: Increased consumers' expenses.
choices.zh: 消费者支出增加。

choices.text: Greater risk of chronic diseases.
choices.zh: 慢性疾病风险增大。

choices.text: People's misunderstanding of nutrition.
choices.zh: 人们对营养的误解。

choices.text: Children's dislike for unprocessed foods.
choices.zh: 儿童不喜欢未加工食品。

items.stem: What do psychologists say people do when they are short of resources?

choices.text: They begin to think of the benefits of constraints.
choices.zh: 他们开始思考约束的好处。

choices.text: They try to seek solutions from creative people.
choices.zh: 他们试图从有创造力的人那里寻求解决方案。

choices.text: They try hard to maximize their mental energy.
choices.zh: 他们努力最大化自己的心理能量。

choices.text: They begin to see the world in a different way.
choices.zh: 他们开始以不同的方式看待世界。

items.stem: What does the passage say about innovation?

choices.text: It is characteristic of all creative people.
choices.zh: 这是所有有创造力的人的特征。

choices.text: It is essential to pushing society forward.
choices.zh: 这对推动社会前进至关重要。

choices.text: It is a creative person's response to limitation.
choices.zh: 这是有创造力的人对限制的回应。

choices.text: It is an impetus to socio-economic development.
choices.zh: 这是社会经济发展的推动力。

items.stem: What did a 2015 study by Ravi Mehta and Meng Zhu find?

choices.text: Scarcity or abundance of resources has little impact on people's creativity.
choices.zh: 资源的稀缺或充裕对人们的创造力影响很小。

choices.text: Innovative people are not constrained in connecting unrelated concepts.
choices.zh: 创新型人才在连接不相关概念时不受约束。

choices.text: People have no incentive to use available resources in new ways.
choices.zh: 人们没有动力以新方式使用可用资源。

choices.text: Creative people tend to consume more available resources.
choices.zh: 有创造力的人往往会消耗更多可用资源。

items.stem: What did Marissa Mayer once write concerning creativity?

choices.text: It is key to a company's survival.
choices.zh: 这是公司生存的关键。

choices.text: It shapes and focuses problems.
choices.zh: 它塑造并聚焦问题。

choices.text: It is essential to meeting challenges
choices.zh: 它对应对挑战至关重要。

choices.text: It thrives best when constrained.
choices.zh: 它在受到约束时最为繁荣。

items.stem: Why does the speaker say strategies for managing conflicts can always be changed?

choices.text: Because they are learned.
choices.zh: 因为它们是习得的。

choices.text: Because they come naturally.
choices.zh: 因为它们是自然而然产生的。

choices.text: Because they have to be properly personalized.
choices.zh: 因为它们必须被适当地个性化。

choices.text: Because there can be more effective strategies.
choices.zh: 因为可能存在更有效的策略。

items.stem: What is said to affect the way one acts in a conflict?

choices.text: The extent of difference and of similarity between the two sides.
choices.zh: 双方之间差异和相似的程度。

choices.text: The knowledge of the specific expectation the other side holds.
choices.zh: 对另一方所持特定期望的了解。

choices.text: The importance of one's goals and of the relationship.
choices.zh: 一个人的目标和关系的重要性。

choices.text: The approaches one adopts to conflict management.
choices.zh: 一个人采用的冲突管理方法。

items.stem: Of the five styles the speaker discusses, which views conflicts as problems to be solved?

choices.text: The fox.
choices.zh: 狐狸型。

choices.text: The owl.
choices.zh: 猫头鹰型。

choices.text: The shark.
choices.zh: 鲨鱼型。

choices.text: The turtle.
choices.zh: 乌龟型。

items.stem: What do scientists hope to do by cracking the genetic code of plants and animals?

choices.text: Help save species from extinction and boost human health.
choices.zh: 帮助拯救物种免于灭绝并促进人类健康。

choices.text: Understand how plants and animals perished over the past.
choices.zh: 了解动植物在过去是如何灭亡的。

choices.text: Help gather information publicly available to researchers.
choices.zh: 帮助收集研究人员可公开获取的信息。

choices.text: Find out the cause of extinction of Britain's 66, 000 species.
choices.zh: 找出英国66000个物种灭绝的原因。

items.stem: What do many scientists believe with regard to earth?

choices.text: It was once dominated by dinosaurs.
choices.zh: 它曾经由恐龙统治。

choices.text: It has entered the sixth mass extinction.
choices.zh: 它已进入第六次大灭绝。

choices.text: Its prospects depend on future human behaviour.
choices.zh: 它的前景取决于人类未来的行为。

choices.text: Its climate change is aggravated by humans.
choices.zh: 它的气候变化因人类而加剧。

items.stem: How does Sir Jim Smith, Director of Science at Wellcome, describe the Darwin Tree of Life Project?

choices.text: It dwarfs all other efforts to conserve, protect and restore biodiversity on earth.
choices.zh: 它使地球上所有其他保护、保护和恢复生物多样性的努力都相形见绌。

choices.text: It is costly to get started and requires the joint efforts of thousands of scientists.
choices.zh: 它启动成本高昂,需要数千名科学家的共同努力。

choices.text: It can help to bring back the large numbers of plants and animals that have gone extinct.
choices.zh: 它可以帮助恢复已经灭绝的大量动植物。

choices.text: It is the most exciting, most relevant, most timely and most internationally inspirational.
choices.zh: 它是最激动人心、最相关、最及时和最具国际启发性的。

items.stem: What is indeed just an illusion according to Professor Tom Oliver?

choices.text: Cultural identity.
choices.zh: 文化身份。

choices.text: Social evolution.
choices.zh: 社会演化。

choices.text: The Copernican revolution.
choices.zh: 哥白尼革命。

choices.text: Human individuality.
choices.zh: 人类个体性。

items.stem: What does Professor Tom Oliver think of the idea that we exist as independent selves at the centre of a subjective universe?

choices.text: It is a delusion to be disposed of.
choices.zh: 这是一种应当被摒弃的错觉。

choices.text: It is prevalent even among academics.
choices.zh: 即使在学术界这种观念也很普遍。

choices.text: It is a myth spread by John Donne's poem.
choices.zh: 这是一个由John Donne的诗歌传播的谬误。

choices.text: It is rooted in the mindset of the 17th century.
choices.zh: 这根植于17世纪的思维模式。

items.stem: Why does Professor Tom Oliver claim that the material "us" is constantly changing?

choices.text: He believes in Copernican philosophical doctrines about the universe.
choices.zh: 他信奉哥白尼关于宇宙的哲学学说。

choices.text: He has gained ample scientific evidence at the University of Reading.
choices.zh: 他在Reading大学获得了充分的科学证据。

choices.text: He has found that our inner self and material self are interconnected.
choices.zh: 他发现我们的内在自我与物质自我是相互关联的。

choices.text: He contends most of our body cells can only live a few days or weeks.
choices.zh: 他认为我们身体的大部分细胞只能存活几天或几周。

items.stem: How can we solve pressing environmental and societal problems according to Professor Tom Oliver?

choices.text: By coming to see how disruptive such problems have got to be.
choices.zh: 通过认识到这些问题已经变得多么具有破坏性。

choices.text: By realising that we all can do our own bit in such endeavours.
choices.zh: 通过意识到我们都可以在这些努力中尽自己的一份力。

choices.text: By becoming aware that we are part of a bigger world.
choices.zh: 通过认识到我们是更大世界的一部分。

choices.text: By making joint efforts resolutely and persistently.
choices.zh: 通过坚决而持续地共同努力。
